title: An adaptive-step audit and a fair experiment
promptMarkdown: For scalar gradients g₁=2, g₂=−1, initialise m₀=s₀=0 and use Adam conventions β₁=.9,β₂=.99,η=.1,ε=0 for this nonzero-denominator calculation. Compute m, s, bias-corrected values and parameter increments at both steps. Then write a small standard-library program comparing GD and the stated momentum method on diag(1,100) for 100 steps from(1,1), with predetermined settings GDη=.01; momentumη=.02,β=.8. Record loss and nonfinite states, verify GD against its exact formula, and explain what this comparison can establish. Give a train/validation/test protocol for choosing settings on a real dataset.
hintLadder: Bias-correction exponents use the actual time index.
The moving squared gradient is a second moment, not a centred variance.
Keep numerical-objective evidence separate from population performance.
